question.problem: Consider the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{k} \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Given that $u\cdot v=6$ and $‖v‖=2$, what is the smallest possible value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality,

$$
|u\cdot v|\le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖.
$$

We are given all the quantities in the inequality above, except for $‖u‖.$ So first, we compute $‖u‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u‖ & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{k})^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{k+3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|u\cdot v| & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖ \\ |6| & \le \sqrt{k+3}\cdot (2) \\ 3 & \le \sqrt{k+3} \\ {3}^{2} & \le (\sqrt{k+3})^{2} \\ 9 & \le k+3 \\ 6 & \le k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $k$ is $6.$
